content: Do not take perindopril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as perindopril can cause harm to the developing fetus. It belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. This medication works by preventing the production of certain natural substances that constrict blood vessels, thereby allowing blood to flow more easily. Perindopril is available in tablet form and is taken orally, usually once or twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about additional uses, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting perindopril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other ACE inhibitors, such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, quinapril, ramipril, or trandolapril. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Inform your doctor if you are undergoing dialysis or if you have a history of heart failure, lupus, scleroderma, diabetes, angioedema (swelling of the face, throat, or extremities), or kidney or liver disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If your doctor has recommended a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. Avoid using potassium-containing salt substitutes without consulting your doctor. If you miss a dose of perindopril, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Perindopril may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience mild symptoms such as cough, headache, weakness, dizziness, diarrhea, stomach pain, or nausea, especially if they persist or worsen. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty swallowing or breathing; lightheadedness; fainting; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; or irregular or rapid heartbeats. If you notice any unusual symptoms while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store perindopril in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical appointments while taking this medication. Do not share it with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Perindopril is sold under the brand name Aceon®.
